steps.note: Intermediate Algebra supplies the real-number/expression/equation machinery that forms Chapter 1 (“Fundamentals”) of the Precalculus text — near-total seam overlap.
Precalculus delivers the functions, trigonometry and log/exponential library that Stewart’s Calculus assumes on page one; only limits are new.
Stewart teaches every computational technique (limits, derivatives, integrals, series) that Apostol re-derives with proofs, so the jump is purely in rigor, not topic.
Apostol’s rigorous continuity, sequences/series and its integrated linear algebra cover Rudin PMA’s opening chapters; Rudin advances into metric-space topology.
Rudin PMA’s metric spaces, Riemann–Stieltjes integral and sequences of functions are exactly the assumed background for Rudin RCA, which advances to Lebesgue measure and complex analysis.
RCA’s measure/integration, Lᵖ and Hilbert/Banach basics overlap Folland’s core, which advances into abstract point-set topology and fuller functional analysis.
Folland’s functional analysis, Lᵖ and distribution groundwork feed directly into Brezis, which advances to Sobolev spaces and PDE — a genuine graduate sink.

lineages.label: Higher-overlap real-analysis on-ramp
lineages.note: Routes through Velleman’s proof techniques and Abbott’s motivated ε-δ analysis, which maximizes the seam into Rudin PMA — the recommended path for a student who has not yet written proofs.

register.title: Woods Advanced Calculus last edition [VERIFIED, noted]
register.body: A 1934 “New edition” (Ginn; LC QA303.W885 1934) exists beyond the 1926 first edition; both catalogued, node dropped by the quality gate. No unresolved bibliographic uncertainty remains.

register.title: No open topical gap
register.body: No invented bridge was required; the proof-transition seam is closed by Velleman (N09) and the Tier-4 first-analysis set (Ross/Abbott/Spivak). Every node resolved to a specific edition and year; the only formerly-unverified item (N07 Stewart–Kokoska) is now confirmed as 5th ed., ©2023 (Cengage, ISBN 9780357632499).

caveats.title: Overlap is structural, never numeric
caveats.body: All seam-overlap claims are inferred from tables of contents, stated prerequisites and published reviews (tagged EVIDENCED) or from reasoned pedagogical judgment where evidence underdetermines the call (JUDGMENT) — never from full-text comparison or invented percentages.

caveats.title: Edition currency
caveats.body: Axler’s 4th ed. carries a 2024 copyright; some retail pages list 2023 (print release). Stewart Calculus 9e is dated 2020 with a 2021 copyright. Stewart–Kokoska is confirmed 5th ed. ©2023. These are catalog-page facts and can shift with reprints.

caveats.title: Parallel-set edges are shared, not sequenced
caveats.body: Within each parallel set no A→B ordering is implied; siblings inherit the same incoming and outgoing edges.

caveats.title: Judgment edges from the Ashlock set
caveats.body: N03–N05 → N08/N09 reflect that these concise “Fast Start” volumes cover derivative/integral/multivariable material at lower depth than Stewart; a student using only the Ashlock path may need supplementary problem sets before Apostol.

caveats.title: The complex-analysis trio are terminal leaves
caveats.body: N21/N22/N23 are not dead ends pedagogically — they represent a parallel graduate specialization rather than a step toward the functional-analysis sinks; a learner may pursue the complex branch and the measure/functional branch independently after Rudin PMA.

caveats.title: Woods (N18) verified but dropped
caveats.body: Included in the bibliography for completeness and because the seed list requested resolution of its edition (1926 first / 1934 new edition).
